name: Rongmei Naga
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Singh, Thangjam Naor 2012. A grammar of Rongmei. Manipur University, Canchipur. xiii+408pp; also Tiwari, S.K. 1971. A descriptive grammar of Kabui. Deccan College.

sources.note: No dialect sub-languoids; alternative names Kabui, Kabiu, Ruangmei, Nruanghmei, Maruongmai, Rongmai.

sources.citation: Ibopishak Singh, P. 1990. Kabui (Rongmei) Grammar. Imphal: Directorate for the Development of Tribals and Backward Classes, Govt. of Manipur. xv+214 pp.
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: open copy online
sources.note: Nothing; the book has no phonology (foreword: 'He has left the phonology, for he wanted to study it separately'); morphology/syntax of Ragailong (Minuthong) village, Imphal. scanned grep for stress/accent/tone: only a symbols-list entry 'Rising tone / Falling tone'.

sources.citation: Tiwari, Surendra Kumar. 1971. Descriptive grammar of Kabui. PhD thesis, Deccan College, Poona (guide D.N. Shankara Bhat). xiii+283 pp. [Shodhganga hdl 10603/173645]
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Nothing. p. 1: 28 phonemes, 27 segmental and one suprasegmental; p. 17 '2.3 Tone: Phonetically there is a two-fold contrast of tones: high-falling and low-falling. On the basis of this contrast a suprasegmental phoneme of high falling tone / ´ / has been set up. It occurs medially and finally with vowels.' No stress in ch. I (48 pp).

sources.citation: Raguibou, I.D. 2015. The Comparative Phonology of Zeme, Liangmai and Rongmei. PhD thesis, Department of Linguistics, Assam University, Silchar (guide Kh. Dhiren Singha). xi+203 pp. [Shodhganga hdl 10603/293375]
sources.note: Nothing. Rongmei section 3.3 (pp. 82-111); 3.3.7 Tone p. 110: 'There are three contrastive tones in Rongmei. They are high, mid (unmark) and low' (Table 21 tone distribution). No stress/accent in the 93 scanned pages of ch. 3 nor in chs. 4-5 or abstract.

sources.citation: Haokip, Pauthang. 2014. Phonology of Rongmei. Language in India 14(4): 196-210 (Cachar/Silchar dialect).
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 4 Tone: 'The current analysis posits two tones in Rongmei, viz. high and low tones'; established in monosyllables only, 'tonal behavior of disyllabic, affixes and phrases have not analysed'. No mention of stress.

sources.citation: Gonmei, Guigongpou. 2010. Typological characteristics of Rongmei. PhD thesis, Department of Linguistics, North-Eastern Hill University, Shillong (guide Juanita War). ix+162 pp. [Shodhganga hdl 10603/60919]
sources.note: No Rongmei stress statement. Ch. 3 Phonological Typology pp. 40-80; 3.4 Suprasegmentals contains only 3.4.1 Tone (three registered tones high/mid/low, tone sandhi, pp. 76-79). Only incidental 'Rongmei has 10 short unstressed oral diphthongs' (p. 67) and a general typology chart (Fig. 5, after Marina 2007) listing predictable/unpredictable stress as types, not applied to Rongmei.
Consonant and vowel tables only; nothing on tone or stress; cites Tiwari 1971.

sources.citation: Singh, Thangjam Naor. 2012. Rongmei Grammar. PhD thesis, Department of Linguistics, Manipur University, Canchipur (guide Ch. Yashawanta Singh). i-xiii, 1-408 pp. [= the scan's 'A grammar of Rongmei'; Shodhganga hdl 10603/534450]
sources.note: Nothing. Ch. II Phonology (pp. 16-64) lists supra-segmental phonemes as tone and juncture only (p. 16); 2.6 Tone: two tones, mid (unmarked) and low (p. 60-62); 2.7 Juncture; conclusion p. 63 'supra-segmental features of two tones as well as juncture'. No stress/accent anywhere in the 50 scanned pages.
